quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part gives you less protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.
Yield to any car already in the roundabout.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and cars already in the roundabout.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Go if you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must let any pedestrian in the intersection cross first. Wait until they have fully crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: When approaching a T intersection, drivers should:
questions.explanation: When you are on the street ending at the T intersection, you must stop and yield to traffic crossing in front of you. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what must you do?

options.text: Only yield if you are at a corner.

questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog shows a person is blind or partially blind. Always yield the right-of-way to someone using either of these.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs hurt reaction time, coordination, alertness, and the ability to focus. All of these are needed for safe driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a winding road ahead.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure they see you before going.
Stop and let them finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down, what should you do?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and get off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and get off the road.
questions.explanation: Get your vehicle off the road if possible. Turn on emergency flashers so other drivers can see you have a problem.

questions.question: When should you change lanes?

options.text: When a car is in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and carefully, only when needed. Every lane change increases your accident risk.

questions.question: A school bus ahead is stopped in your lane with red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the lights flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped while the lights flash.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. You do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area set aside for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians can cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians can cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are often marked with white lines. They may be marked or unmarked.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.
When there is a red traffic light.

questions.explanation: Stop at a red traffic light. Always obey a police officer directing traffic, regardless of signs or signals.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an octagonal sign?
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe.

questions.question: Your reaction time slows after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and other vehicles.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: Front seat passengers and passengers age 16 or younger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Front seat passengers and passengers age 16 or younger.
questions.explanation: In Arizona, all front seat passengers must wear a fastened safety belt. Passengers age 16 or younger must also wear a fastened safety belt, no matter where they sit in the vehicle.

questions.question: When rain or fog reduces visibility, you should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off precipitation and bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: As daylight fades, what should you use so others can see you?
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades. Use high beams only in open areas with no other drivers present.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off weather conditions and reduce visibility even more.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive under ideal conditions. Drive at the same speed as surrounding traffic, up to the limit. All drivers must maintain a safe speed at all times.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off weather and make visibility worse.

questions.question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light is in their favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the circumstances.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Signal before every lane change to alert other drivers. Always check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers of a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: You see a pedestrian crossing your lane ahead with no crosswalk. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: At uncontrolled intersections, yield to pedestrians in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Yield to pedestrians even if there is no crosswalk.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.

questions.explanation: Stay at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts your life and the rider's life at risk. If the rider falls, you need extra distance to avoid them. Falls are most likely on wet roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges or railroad tracks.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep a constant speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Drive carefully near railroad tracks.

questions.question: This white sign means you should not pass other vehicles:

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.

questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign means you must obey the rule. This sign means do not pass other vehicles for any reason.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction and work areas?
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: How should head restraints be adjusted?

options.text: So it touches the back of your head.
Remove them from the seats if possible.
Position does not matter since they have no effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: So it touches the back of your head.
questions.explanation: Head restraints prevent whiplash from rear-end crashes. Adjust them so the head restraint touches the back of your head.
